answer: One identity per network origin. Each agent binds its key to an ASN and /24; the ledger rejects any new identity sharing an origin with an active one, so a comet of clones cannot hide behind one network. Each origin locks 200 POA for the epoch, refunded at close, slashed if a challenger proves two keys share one origin, challenger keeps half. A thousand aliases means leasing a thousand ASNs, $2,000/month, plus two hundred thousand POA locked, burned on any duplicate. Like a juniper that grows one to a ridge, each origin holds one identity; crowding it is washed out with the tide.
